chunks: The prophet Dāwūd (David), peace be upon him, rose up at a similar hour one night and said, “This is the hour when whatever a person prays for is granted to him unless he is a tax-collector, an intelligence man, a police officer, a lute player or a drummer.”
ai.seo_question: What conditions prevent a supplication from being answered during the preferred night hours?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual potency of the 'hour of acceptance' in the latter part of the night, drawing a parallel to Prophet David’s (peace be upon him) practice. This narration underscores the concept of *istijabah* (answering of prayers) while noting that specific worldly occupations—such as tax collection or music-playing—can act as veils preventing the supplicant's voice from reaching the Divine, reflecting the Shia emphasis on purifying one's state and duties during worship.
